WTI +9.42% to $78.14 while XLE sits at $55.08 represents lagged sector catch-up; Brent pushed above $83 after hours as the blockade goes live Tuesday 4pm ET. High-oil, rising-yield regime inflects energy FCF strongly; geopolitical premium may prove stickier than consensus.

bear_case: Counter-argument: Iran oil spikes historically mean-revert within 48-72 hours once diplomatic channels open or markets recognize the Strait of Hormuz disruption is a tariff, not supply destruction. The 30Y at 5.101% is +3bps from Friday, not the +12bps shock of May 15. June CPI will capture a month when WTI fell ~10%, likely printing headline negative MoM and ~3.8% YoY — a meaningful beat of the 4.2% May level. Consensus expects -0.1% MoM / 3.8% YoY, with core at ~2.9% — if it prints at or below consensus the risk-off tone reverses fast. TSMC's June revenue tonight (+67.9% YoY) signals AI chip demand remains robust and could be the catalyst that overcomes the geopolitical narrative if CPI cooperates. Banks reporting strong Q2 NII and resilient credit would replicate the May 20 BUY upgrade dynamic where the Step Aside resolved in three sessions. VIX at 16.89 has not confirmed regime break. Invalidation level: if SPX reclaims 7,600 by Wednesday with VIX below 17 and 30Y retreating below 4.90%, the Iran shock was a one-day overshoot and the call is wrong.
